newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks drift up on cautious dealing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks drift up on cautious dealing.

text.p: Mexican stocks posted steady gains on Monday after a low volume session hallmarked by caution and same-day buy-sell trading, dealers said.
"The market was very conservative and there was much quick in-and-out trading. Nonetheless, we also saw some selective buying in the wake of the (1996 earnings) reports," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 35.05 points, or 0.92 percent, at 3,844.80. Trading volume was dull at 59.2 million shares.

Analysts said that same-day buy-sell trading was a symptom of uncertainty among investors, who still await developments in the money and foreign exchange markets, to say nothing of the political situation.
"An excess of (in-and-out) trades may be observed, which indicates market uncertainty," a report from the Valburmex brokerage said.

Dealers said the U.S. Congressional debate on certifying Mexico's effort in the war on drugs and the Houston trial of former special prosecutor Mario Ruiz Massieu were casting shadows on the political front.

A civil action began on Monday to confiscate some $9 million in bank deposits by Ruiz Massieu, which U.S. prosecutors allege comes from bribes paid by drug traffickers. Ruiz Massieu said in court filings that the money came from a family fortune made in real estate.
Another analyst said that, despite caution, some selective buying was visible as dealers began to juggle portfolios in the wake of 1996 earnings reports.
"Investors have improved strategies now all the (1996 earnings) reports have been posted," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with the Bursametrica consultancy.
"They are stepping into the market, albeit cautiously. Furthermore, stocks are now cheaper in dollar terms," he added.
Traders noted that a record-breaking close on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones rose 1.12 percent to 7,079.39 points, helped shore up share prices in Mexico.
On the broad market, 111 stocks changed owners and gains outnumbered declines 51 to 30.
Debt-stricken holding company Sidek headed the gains list on what traders said was a technical rebound after a sharp fall on Friday.
Sidek was followed by its tourist arm Situr and its steelmaking subsidiary Simec.
Dealers said the stocks also recovered on news creditor banks had extended the maturity of an emergency credit line until June 30.
Sidek B shares gained 12 centavos to 60 centavos, Situr ended up seven centavos at 29 centavos and Simec was up 21 centavos at 1.55 pesos.
Mining firm Penoles also gained strongly, up 1.85 pesos to 38.35 pesos, on news of growth in its output and sales of gold, silver, lead and zinc.
Traders said prominent decliners ended down after light dealing that did not reflect market trends.
